table_result.overview: This table stores information about customer support interactions. It tracks individual requests for assistance. The data supports analysis of customer service operations. It helps in understanding the volume and nature of customer inquiries. This table is essential for monitoring and improving customer support efficiency.

fields.name: channel
fields.description: This column indicates the communication method used for the support ticket.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: This column contains a numerical value representing the urgency level of the support ticket.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description: This column contains a unique identifier for each support ticket.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: This column holds the unique identifier for the customer associated with the support ticket.

fields.name: created_date
fields.description: This column stores the date when the support ticket was created.

queries.sql:
WITH DailyHighPriorityTickets AS (
  SELECT
    created_date,
    FORMAT_DATE('%A', created_date) AS day_of_week,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS high_priority_ticket_count
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  WHERE priority = 1
  GROUP BY created_date
),
WeeklyAverageHighPriority AS (
  SELECT
    day_of_week,
    AVG(high_priority_ticket_count) AS avg_high_priority_ticket_count
  FROM DailyHighPriorityTickets
  GROUP BY day_of_week
)
SELECT
  d.created_date,
  d.day_of_week,
  d.high_priority_ticket_count,
  w.avg_high_priority_ticket_count
FROM DailyHighPriorityTickets AS d
JOIN WeeklyAverageHighPriority AS w
  ON d.day_of_week = w.day_of_week
WHERE d.high_priority_ticket_count > w.avg_high_priority_ticket_count * 1.5 -- 50% above average as anomaly threshold
ORDER BY d.created_date DESC;
queries.description: Identify days where the number of high-priority (priority = 1) tickets is significantly higher than the average number of high-priority tickets for that day of the week, indicating a potential anomaly in workload.

queries.sql:
WITH DailyChannelTickets AS (
  SELECT
    created_date,
    channel,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS daily_ticket_count
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  GROUP BY created_date, channel
),
ChannelRollingAverage AS (
  SELECT
    created_date,
    channel,
    daily_ticket_count,
    AVG(daily_ticket_count) OVER (PARTITION BY channel ORDER BY UNIX_DATE(created_date) RANGE BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS seven_day_avg_ticket_count
  FROM DailyChannelTickets
)
SELECT
  created_date,
  channel,
  daily_ticket_count,
  seven_day_avg_ticket_count
FROM ChannelRollingAverage
WHERE daily_ticket_count > seven_day_avg_ticket_count * 2 -- Daily count is more than double the 7-day average
  AND seven_day_avg_ticket_count IS NOT NULL -- Exclude initial days with no 7-day average
ORDER BY created_date DESC, channel;
queries.description: Identify channels that experience a sudden surge in ticket volume on a specific date compared to their typical daily volume, potentially indicating a channel-specific issue or event.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  created_date,
  COVAR_POP(priority, ticket_count) AS priority_ticket_count_covariance
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    created_date,
    AVG(priority) AS priority,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_count
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  GROUP BY
    customer_id,
    created_date
)
GROUP BY
  customer_id,
  created_date
HAVING
  COUNT(ticket_count) > 1;
queries.description: Compute the population covariance between the priority of tickets and the number of tickets created by each customer on a given day, to see if customers who create more tickets also tend to create higher priority tickets.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  CORR(priority, ticket_count) AS priority_ticket_count_correlation
FROM (
  SELECT
    created_date,
    AVG(priority) AS priority,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_count
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  GROUP BY
    created_date
);
queries.description: Calculate the correlation between ticket priority and the number of tickets created on a given date to understand if higher priority issues tend to be reported more frequently on certain days.

queries.sql: SELECT t1.customer_id FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` AS t1 JOIN (SELECT customer_id, MAX(created_date) AS last_ticket_date FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id) AS t2 ON t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id AND t1.created_date = t2.last_ticket_date JOIN (SELECT customer_id, AVG(priority) AS avg_priority FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id) AS t3 ON t1.customer_id = t3.customer_id WHERE t1.priority > t3.avg_priority;
queries.description: Identify customers whose most recent ticket's priority is higher than their average ticket priority across all their tickets.

queries.sql: SELECT created_date, customer_id, priority, AVG(priority) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY created_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS seven_day_moving_avg_priority FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` ORDER BY customer_id, created_date;
queries.description: Calculate the moving average of ticket priority over a 7-day window for each customer.

queries.sql: SELECT customer_id, STDDEV(priority) AS priority_stddev FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY priority_stddev DESC LIMIT 1;
queries.description: Find the customer who has the highest standard deviation in ticket priority across all their tickets.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  FORMAT_DATE('%A', created_date) AS day_of_week,
  VAR_POP(priority) AS daily_priority_variance
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
GROUP BY
  day_of_week
ORDER BY
  daily_priority_variance DESC;
queries.description: Calculate the population variance of ticket priorities for each day of the week to understand daily consistency in reported issue urgency.

queries.sql:
WITH DailyAveragePriority AS (
  SELECT
    created_date,
    AVG(priority) AS average_priority
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  WHERE created_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  GROUP BY created_date
)
SELECT
  created_date,
  average_priority,
  LAG(average_priority, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY created_date) AS previous_day_average_priority,
  average_priority - LAG(average_priority, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY created_date) AS priority_change
FROM DailyAveragePriority
ORDER BY created_date;
queries.description: Analyze the daily trend of average priority for support tickets, highlighting the change compared to the previous day.

queries.sql: SELECT customer_id, APPROX_QUANTILES(priority, 100)[OFFSET(75)] AS p75_priority FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` WHERE created_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) GROUP BY customer_id;
queries.description: Calculate the 75th percentile of ticket priorities for each customer, considering only tickets created in the last 90 days.

queries.sql: SELECT channel, AVG(priority) AS avg_priority FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` WHERE created_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) GROUP BY channel ORDER BY avg_priority DESC LIMIT 3;
queries.description: Identify the top 3 channels with the highest average priority for tickets created in the last year.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  channel,
  AVG(priority) AS average_priority,
  COUNT(ticket_id) AS total_tickets
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
GROUP BY
  channel
ORDER BY
  average_priority DESC
LIMIT 5;
queries.description: Find the top 5 channels that have the highest average ticket priority, along with the count of tickets for each, to identify channels frequently used for urgent issues.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  channel,
  customer_id,
  ticket_count,
  average_priority
FROM (
  SELECT
    channel,
    customer_id,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_count,
    AVG(priority) AS average_priority,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY channel ORDER BY COUNT(ticket_id) DESC) AS rn
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  GROUP BY
    channel,
    customer_id
)
WHERE
  rn <= 3
ORDER BY
  channel,
  ticket_count DESC;
queries.description: For each channel, list the top 3 customers who have created the most tickets, along with the average priority of their tickets within that channel.

queries.sql: SELECT channel, COUNTIF(priority <= 2) * 100.0 / COUNT(ticket_id) AS high_priority_percentage FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY channel;
queries.description: Calculate the percentage of high-priority tickets (priority <= 2) for each channel.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  t.customer_id,
  MAX(t.priority) AS max_priority_across_channels
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` AS t
WHERE
  t.customer_id IN (
    SELECT
      customer_id
    FROM
      `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
    GROUP BY
      customer_id
    HAVING
      COUNT(DISTINCT channel) >= 2
  )
GROUP BY
  t.customer_id;
queries.description: Identify customers who have submitted tickets through at least two different channels and calculate the maximum priority they've ever assigned.

queries.sql: SELECT customer_id, MAX(priority) - MIN(priority) AS priority_range FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(ticket_id) > 1;
queries.description: For each customer, find the difference between their maximum and minimum ticket priority.

queries.sql: SELECT customer_id FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` WHERE priority = 1 GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(ticket_id) >= 5;
queries.description: Identify customers who have submitted at least 5 tickets with a priority of 1.

queries.sql: SELECT CORR(t1.priority, t2.daily_ticket_count) AS priority_ticket_count_correlation FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` AS t1 JOIN (SELECT created_date, customer_id, COUNT(ticket_id) AS daily_ticket_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY created_date, customer_id) AS t2 ON t1.created_date = t2.created_date AND t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id;
queries.description: Calculate the correlation between ticket priority and the number of tickets created by a customer on the same day.

queries.sql: SELECT FORMAT_DATE('%A', created_date) AS day_of_week, AVG(priority) AS avg_priority FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY day_of_week ORDER BY CASE WHEN day_of_week = 'Monday' THEN 1 WHEN day_of_week = 'Tuesday' THEN 2 WHEN day_of_week = 'Wednesday' THEN 3 WHEN day_of_week = 'Thursday' THEN 4 WHEN day_of_week = 'Friday' THEN 5 WHEN day_of_week = 'Saturday' THEN 6 WHEN day_of_week = 'Sunday' THEN 7 END;
queries.description: Find the average priority of tickets for each day of the week, considering all tickets.

queries.sql: SELECT channel, AVG(ticket_count) AS avg_tickets_per_customer_per_channel FROM (SELECT customer_id, channel, COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id, channel HAVING COUNT(ticket_id) > 5) GROUP BY channel;
queries.description: Determine the average number of tickets created per customer per channel, but only for customers who have created more than 5 tickets in total.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers_with_multiple_channels FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT channel) > 1);
queries.description: Determine the number of unique customers who have submitted tickets through more than one channel.

queries.sql: SELECT channel, APPROX_QUANTILES(priority, 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_priority FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets` GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(ticket_id) >= 10) GROUP BY channel;
queries.description: Determine the median priority of tickets for each channel, considering only tickets submitted by customers who have submitted at least 10 tickets in total.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  STDDEV_SAMP(priority) AS priority_stddev
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
GROUP BY
  customer_id
HAVING
  COUNT(ticket_id) > 1;
queries.description: Determine the sample standard deviation of ticket priorities for each customer to identify customers with highly variable support needs.

queries.sql:
WITH MonthlyUniqueCustomers AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC(created_date, MONTH) AS month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS unique_customers
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  WHERE created_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 YEAR) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  month,
  unique_customers,
  SUM(unique_customers) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS cumulative_unique_customers
FROM MonthlyUniqueCustomers
ORDER BY month;
queries.description: Determine the number of unique customers who submitted tickets each month and their cumulative count over time.

queries.sql:
WITH CustomerTicketTimelines AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(created_date) AS first_ticket_date,
    MAX(created_date) AS last_ticket_date
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  WHERE created_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  AVG(DATE_DIFF(last_ticket_date, first_ticket_date, DAY)) AS average_ticket_span_days
FROM CustomerTicketTimelines;
queries.description: Determine the average time difference in days between a customer's first and last ticket submission within a year.

queries.sql:
WITH CustomerTicketCounts AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS total_tickets
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.support_tickets`
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
OverallTicketStats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(total_tickets) AS avg_tickets_per_customer,
    STDDEV(total_tickets) AS stddev_tickets_per_customer
  FROM CustomerTicketCounts
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.total_tickets,
  o.avg_tickets_per_customer,
  o.stddev_tickets_per_customer
FROM CustomerTicketCounts AS c
CROSS JOIN OverallTicketStats AS o
WHERE c.total_tickets > o.avg_tickets_per_customer + (2 * o.stddev_tickets_per_customer) -- More than 2 standard deviations above average
ORDER BY c.total_tickets DESC;
queries.description: Find customer IDs that have an unusually high number of tickets compared to the average customer, potentially indicating a problematic customer or a customer experiencing recurring issues.
